title: Troponin I (cardiac)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Troponin is a protein found in heart muscle cells. Blood normally contains so little that only sensitive tests can detect it. Troponin I and troponin T are two types; a lab may measure either.
context: Troponin can take a few hours to rise, so the test is often repeated over 12 to 24 hours. Biotin (vitamin B7) supplements can make results appear lower than they really are.
aboveRange: Stress or strain on the heart muscle, from several possible heart conditions
Heart surgery or a chest injury
Long, intense exercise such as running a marathon
Some kidney or lung conditions, or a serious illness elsewhere in the body
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
